headline: 2-3 on 5 value plays, -$11.82
paragraphs: Week 12 put 5 graded games in front of the model. It found a playable edge in 4 of them and left the other 1 alone. Those plays went 2-3, worth -$11.82 at $10 a play (-23.6% on the $50 at risk).

By market, spreads went 2-2 and the lone moneyline lost. The best of them was Miami (OH) -9.5 in Miami (OH) at Kent State, a 3.5-point disagreement with the market that finished Miami (OH) 20, Kent State 3. The one that stung was Massachusetts -3 in Akron at Massachusetts, a 9.9-point disagreement with the market that finished Akron 34, Massachusetts 33.

The five plays that actually got published went 0-1 for -$10.00, behind the full board. Ranking by expected value is supposed to concentrate the good ones at the top, and whether it does is something only a season of these will answer.

Season to date the model has made 525 value plays and gone 228-282-15, -$598.41 on flat $10 bets (-11.4%). It expected to win 61% of those and won 45%. On line movement, 7 of the 19 published picks whose numbers moved closed worse than the site posted them, so the market came our way 37% of the time. Sample is getting real enough to argue with, though a model that beats closing lines is rarer than one that beats a few hundred results.
